payload.summary: e2e built: tests/e2e/game.test.ts, 3 tests, suite 340 -> 343 green, bunx tsc --noEmit exit 0. No product defect surfaced — the loop, the game master, the client and the CLI already joined up correctly, so the file is all test and no fix.

e2e finding — how a single degraded LLM call is provoked without tripping the breaker. The fake vendor answers one narration call with HTTP 400, not 500: ChatClient#send retries 429/5xx once, so a 500 would take two vendor requests and, if only one were failed by index, the retry would succeed and no fallback would ever be seen. A 400 is not retried, so it is exactly one failed call — GameMaster#guarded counts one consecutive failure, under the LLM_FAILURE_LIMIT of 2, and the session recovers on the next call. The test pins recovery structurally: a vendor-marked narration line exists both BEFORE and AFTER the one-time '(the game master is not answering)' notice, the line immediately after the notice is a plain engine sentence, and 'LLM disabled for this session' never appears.

e2e finding — a WIN is only scriptable because the test computes the case file itself. The screen never shows the answer before the reveal (that is the ADR-0001 property), so the scripted player calls createGame with the same seed and player count and reads state.caseFile, then picks those three cards out of the accusation menus. The alternative — a player who guesses — cannot be relied on to finish, and a game ended by an opponent's deduction never exercises the human seat's accusation path at all. The same known triple then doubles as a leak check: it appears exactly once in the whole transcript, in the reveal, after game over.

e2e finding — the ledger assertion is checked against the vendor's serving side, not restated. The fake vendor pushes every usage object it serves into an array and varies the figures per call (prompt 40+7i, completion 5+3i), so the summed 'LLM usage: N calls, 1 failed attempt, T tokens (P prompt + C completion)' line cannot pass by coincidence; vendor.requests.length is asserted to be served.length + 1, the one extra being the refused call, which contributes attempts but no tokens. Mutation-checked twice: serving usage:null and moving the failing call out of range both fail the test.

e2e finding — the offline process cases run from an mkdtemp cwd, never the repo. loadLlmConfig reads .env.local from the working directory, so a child started in the repo would find the maintainer's real key; the answer script is written into that temp dir and piped in as a file, and POE_API_KEY is emptied in the child env as a second lock. tests/ui/cli.test.ts covers --help, argument errors and one offline game already, so this file adds only what a process pair can show: a scripted game to the reveal from a neutral cwd, and byte-for-byte identical stdout across two separate processes on the same seed with nothing stripped — the transcript carries no clock, no port and no path, and if one ever appears this is the test that says so.
